endorsements.quote: Pharmacists, physicians and other health professionals retain full authority to accept, modify, or reject system-generated recommendations based on clinical judgment, patient context, and interprofessional considerations.
RAG enables LLM to reference up—to-date guideline content, product information, safety communications, and curated evidence repositories at the point of care [27, 28].
To support accountable oversight, recommendations are accompanied by transparent reasoning, linked evidence sources, and concise rationale summaries.
When data are incomplete or evidence is limited, the system should explicitly communicate uncertainty and prompt clinical verification.
All clinician interactions with system-generated recommendations, including over rides, modifications, errors, and adverse events, should be systematically documented.

Deployment within privacy-preserving, jurisdiction-compliant infrastructures and centrally validated, version-controlled updates should ensure regulatory alignment, auditability, and prevention of uncontrolled model drift.
Evaluation should be embedded in system design and initially focus on usability, workflow integration, transparency, and reliability of recommendations.
Only after stable use is demonstrated should evaluation extend to clinical outcomes and patient-level effects.
Implementation is expected to be modular, beginning with deterministic safety rules before integrating more advanced AI components.

unlisted_practices: Use hybrid AI architectures combining retrieval-augmented generation, deterministic safety rules, and LLM reasoning rather than stand-alone LLMs for high-risk pharmacotherapy decision support.
Integrate patient goals, preferences, and treatment burden explicitly into AI-supported pharmacotherapy recommendations.
Include safety guardrails that verify doses, contraindications, and clinically relevant drug-drug interactions in AI-assisted pharmacotherapy.
Constrain continuous learning of AI systems within defined governance structures and avoid autonomous self-optimization.
Involve clinicians in the design, validation, and governance of AI-supported pharmacotherapy decision support.
Decompose clinical activities into distinct tasks so AI support is targeted and indiscriminate automation of complex decisions is avoided.
Prioritize AI-surfaced information by clinical relevance, patient vulnerability, and actionability to reduce alert burden.
Include patients and the public in evaluating AI-supported pharmacotherapy frameworks.

screen.reason: Conceptual framework and design principles paper outlining a hybrid AI framework for pharmacotherapy optimization rather than an empirical evaluation.
